A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, equations, 17 tables, and Appendices A–E. Renamed models and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V3 reports original Shakespeare and OpenWebText experiments, benchmark evaluations, transport-cost measurements, ablations, and a bound-tightness simulation in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of exact-OT BoW training and EMA-based variants.

M1.justification: V4 implements moving-average parameters for computing OT embedding costs, whereas v3 Section 7 only suggested this refinement. The underlying OT objective, multimask construction, training losses, and inference procedures remain. DFM-MMLM becomes DFM-MMF through renaming.

E1.justification: Both versions use character-level and Morse-code Shakespeare, OpenWebText, and the same five language-modeling test sets: LAMBADA, Wikitext2, PTB, Wikitext103, and LM1B. The added variants retain existing tasks and source-distribution scenarios.

E2.justification: The comparisons add DFM-B-Exact and EMA variants. Existing multimask exact-OT results from v3 Appendix C.8 also join the consolidated comparisons in Tables 3, 9–12. SEDD, GPT-2, and the existing masked-flow comparators are retained.

E3.justification: New ablations introduce exact-OT training configurations with and without EMA, using a target decay of 0.99999 and a ramp-up schedule. The existing OWT training budget, sequence length, batch size, generation-step grid, and evaluation models remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: V4 adds an ablation testing whether EMA-based coupling improves BoW and multimask models, including entropy checks. The earlier solver, OT-batch-size, bound-tightness, and transport-cost analyses remain; the multimask exact-solver experiment itself is not new.

E5.justification: Appendix C.4 newly clarifies that standard deviations are calculated across generated samples, not across runs. Existing uncertainty values and reporting conventions are retained, with no newly reported training-seed counts or repeated-run study.

E6.justification: New variants substantially extend the central results. Table 3 reports DFM-B-Exact-EMA at 182.40 with 32 steps versus retained DFM-B at 185.12 with 1024 steps, and DFM-MMF-Exact-EMA at 132.55 with 1024 steps versus DFM-MMF-OT at 141.92. Appendix C.7 changes the reported correlations from 0.96/0.958 to 0.933/0.932. Previously reported corresponding model rows are retained.

T1.justification: V4 repairs the entropy derivation for Proposition 4.3, revises Appendix A.5's exact cross-entropy expression, including changing the source-entropy term from negative to positive, and corrects the mask/data branches in Appendix A.6. The principal OT and perplexity-bound theorems remain, with mostly equivalent notation changes in the main text.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion substantially strengthen the headline efficiency claim from an 8-fold reduction, 1024 to 128 steps, to a 32-fold reduction, 1024 to 32. Section 5 attributes the latter result to the BoW EMA variant. The OT-equivalence, perplexity-bound, and multimask contributions otherwise remain.

C2.justification: V3's coupling/embedding feedback limitation and suggested moving-average remedy become an explanation of instability mitigated by tested EMA training in v4 Section 5.4. The solver discussion also shifts from emphasizing small low-step improvements to describing no significant generative-perplexity change.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds the EMA decay and ramp-up formula, changes the reported GPU from H200 to GH200, and removes the general epsilon-offset scheduler specification without establishing an actual scheduler change. The printed code pointer changes from DFM-OT-B to DFM-OT; repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Appendix C newly identifies the adopted architecture specifically with Lou et al. (2024) and Haxholli et al. (2025), providing more explicit attribution. The bibliography, related-work discussion, and main novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 condenses Remark 3.4, revises bound explanations and model terminology, swaps the ablation and scaling subsections, and incorporates the former limitations discussion into the experiments. It removes the appendix contents page and replaces the LLM usage statement with an impact statement. Most narrative content remains.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column formatting, with extensive changes to typography, headers, equation wrapping, table styling, and placement. Tables 3, 7, 9–12 expand, including redisplayed appendix results. All seven generated-sample listings remain; neither version contains numbered figures.

improvement.justification: V4 turns v3's suggested stability remedy into documented, controlled EMA experiments and repairs several mathematical derivations, strengthening the evidence and correctness. These gains outweigh limited documentation drawbacks: the scheduler disclosure disappears, and the new MMF-EMA 64-step result differs between Tables 3 and 10, 156.62 versus 156.52. The overall improvement is incremental within the retained research scope.
